Sept. 25: Friday's news to know
By Todd Zola

The New York Yankees have joined the Boston Red Sox in scheduling a doubleheader today, hoping to get their weekend series in with a pending Nor'easter expected to bring heavy rain and winds throughout most of the weekend. The Red Sox and Chicago Cubs kick off the action at 1:05 p.m. ET in the first game of their split twin bill. The Yankees and Baltimore Orioles will get started with their single-admission doubleheader at 4:05 p.m. ET.

The Cleveland Guardians enter today's festivities assured of a playoff berth, but they still have a lot to play for since they are only one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox for the AL Central title, with the division winner earning a first-round bye. The Guardians spend the weekend on the road against the Kansas City Royals while the White Sox host the Colorado Rockies.
The AL West champion is still up in the air with the Texas Rangers and Houston Astros tied heading into the final weekend. The Astros hold the tiebreaker if the Lone Star State denizens end the season with the same record. The Astros visit the Athletics while the Rangers are on the road against the Minnesota Twins.
There is also one unresolved spot in the Senior Circuit with the Philadelphia Phillies currently two games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks for the final wild-card berth. The Diamondbacks finish the season on the road against the San Diego Padres. Arizona would win the potential tiebreaker over Philadelphia.
The Phillies may have to fend off the Diamondbacks without Luis Arraez. Not only are the clubs battling for the final NL playoff berth, but Arraez enters the weekend a mere .002 points ahead of Diamondbacks catcher Gabriel Moreno for the batting average crown. Arraez's status is pending an evaluation today, though the outlook for the weekend is bleak.
The Red Sox avoided a scare with Ceddanne Rafaela returning to last night's lineup after having left the previous game due to a leg issue. It was determined that he just experienced cramping. On the other hand, the prognosis on Willson Contreras is worrisome. He may not play the rest of the regular season and could miss the Wild Card Series.
The Astros placed Daulton Varsho on the 10-day IL as a result of an inflamed left wrist. The stint was backdated, but he'll still be ineligible for the Wild Card Series if the Astros win the AL West. Varsho would be eligible to return for the ALDS.
Dalton Rushing is set to be activated from the 10-day IL after missing almost three months thanks to a sore right elbow. He'll serve as the Los Angeles Dodgers' reserve catcher, but the club may try to get him some reps over the regular season's final three games.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Friday.

Sept. 24: Thursday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The final Thursday of the regular season is a relatively busy one, with a dozen games -- five in the afternoon and seven in the evening. Action commences at 12:35 p.m. ET when the Pittsburgh Pirates host the St. Louis Cardinals.

The weather should cooperate today, but the weekend ahead could be a mess with a Nor'easter expected to have some impact. MLB has already made one schedule change, with the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs playing a doubleheader on Friday. They'll hope to be able to play their Game 162 on Saturday. The Red Sox are in the playoffs, while the Cubs' fate is still currently in limbo.
The Chicago White Sox enter today's game one game behind the Cleveland Guardians in the AL Central. However, if the White Sox beat the Kansas City Royals this afternoon, they will clinch a playoff berth.
The Phillies host the Milwaukee Brewers this evening. The Brewers are two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for home-field advantage throughout the National League playoffs, but the Phillies are still aiming to lock down a playoff spot. A win gets it done.
The San Diego Padres enter tonight's meeting with the Dodgers one game ahead of both the Phillies and Cubs for the top NL wild card. Both of those teams hold the tiebreaker edge over the Padres. San Diego ends the season against the Arizona Diamondbacks. If the Padres are swept, they could miss out on the postseason. Arizona meets the Colorado Rockies this afternoon in the final game of the season at Coors Field, then heads to San Diego for three potentially crucial contests.
The Red Sox and Guardians meet today in the final game of their series at Fenway Park. The Red Sox hope to have Ceddanne Rafaela in the lineup after he had to leave last night's game early. The initial report is leg cramping, but he's set for an MRI today.
The Guardians will open with right-hander Daniel Espino, then bring in Joey Cantillo as the bulk reliever. The move will force Red Sox manager Chad Tracy to make a few decisions, since they've been using a few platoons.
Ronald Acuna Jr. missed last night's game, but the Atlanta Braves indicated that the absence was precautionary. The star outfielder had left Tuesday's contest after fouling a ball off his left shin. X-rays were negative, and Acuna wanted to play, but with their playoff seed wrapped up, the club took the safe route.
The Seattle Mariners have not been mathematically eliminated from the postseason, but they need to sweep their series against the Los Angeles Angels, beginning tonight at home, and then get a lot of losses from the two teams ahead of them in the standings. The Texas Rangers begin play today tied with the Houston Astros atop the AL West. However, the Astros hold the tiebreaker between those two teams.
Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena missed last night's game after being hit in the wrist by a pitch on Tuesday night. He's questionable for tonight's road affair with the Athletics.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli hits wall and suffers early exit from Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying
stories.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is set to start 16th on the grid at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after hitting the wall at Turn 1 and damaging his car beyond repair in the opening session of qualifying on Friday.
stories.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is set to start 16th on the grid at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after hitting the wall at Turn 1 and damaging his car beyond repair in the opening session of qualifying on Friday.

The Mercedes driver was on his second flying lap of the Q1 session when he clipped the wall on the apex of Turn 1 and damaged the front left corner of his car.

Antonelli initially tried to return to the pits, but his race engineer, Peter Bonnington, informed him to park the car at a safe point further round the lap.

"That looks like we've done something to the trackrod and upright, so that's a fairly big job," Antonelli was told after he pleaded with Bonnington to return to the pits for repairs.

The 20-year-old's initial lap in Q1 was good enough to secure the 15th fastest time of the session, meaning he made the cut for Q2 even though he was unable to take part in it.

As he watched on from the behind the crash barriers near where he stopped his car, Antonelli contemplated the reality of starting in the bottom half of the grid for Saturday's grand prix.

- Max Verstappen pips George Russell in closing stages of Azerbaijan GP final practice

- F1 teams to expect decision on Qatar, Abu Dhabi and where 2026 season will end by mid-October

- Christian Horner on F1 return: Ferrari team principal would be 'the dream'

The Italian currently has an 81-point lead over teammate George Russell in the championship and is still on target to cruise towards his first F1 title in just his second year in the category.

The qualifying crash will be a setback, but Antonelli will likely be buoyed by the fact he won from 19th on the grid at the Italian Grand Prix earlier this month.

Antonelli had experienced a disrupted Thursday practice in Baku after a hydraulic leak on his power unit caused him to lose track time at the end of FP1 and the start of FP2.

stories.headline: Lapsed fan's guide to the NHL season: Top teams, players, storylines for 2026-27
stories.summary: Miss anything since the end of June? Miss EVERYTHING since then? Get caught up here.
stories.body:
The 2025-26 NHL season was a heck of a ride. Especially for Jaccob Slavin.

The veteran defenseman played a key role for the U.S. men's Olympic hockey team, which defeated Canada for its first gold medal since the 1980 Miracle on Ice as the NHL returned to the Winter Games.

A few months later, Slavin became just the second American-born player -- and ninth player overall -- to win Olympic gold and the Stanley Cup in the same season, as the Carolina Hurricanes eliminated the Vegas Golden Knights and hoisted the chalice for the first time since 2006.

Then the real fun began in the NHL, with one of the most drama-filled and unpredictable offseasons in recent history.

If you haven't kept up with the NHL in the past few months, don't fret, we've got you covered. Here's a chance to catch up on everything that has happened -- the hirings, firings, signings, trades and the unfinished stories that could reach intense conclusions.

It's all in our guide to the 2026-27 season for lapsed fans. Read up before the puck drops!

The Stanley Cup favorites
The Hurricanes will try to become the fourth team in the last 11 seasons to repeat as Stanley Cup champions, but it's not going to be easy. The Florida Panthers, the last team to go back-to-back (2024, 2025), are back with a vengeance after injuries derailed their push for a three-peat to the point that they missed the playoffs entirely.

Over in the Western Conference, the Colorado Avalanche are once again the favorites after finishing with the league's best record in 2025-26. Right behind them are the Edmonton Oilers, as stars Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl attempt to carry their team to a third Stanley Cup Final appearance in four seasons.

Here are the top contenders based on their DraftKings odds to win the Stanley Cup, as of Thursday:

Florida Panthers +650
Carolina Hurricanes +650
Colorado Avalanche +700
Edmonton Oilers +800
Vegas Golden Knights +850
Tampa Bay Lightning +1000
Minnesota Wild +1300
Dallas Stars +1400
Washington Capitals +1700

Also of note: the Montreal Canadiens (+2200), who were Eastern Conference finalists last season; the New Jersey Devils, Los Angeles Kings and Buffalo Sabres all at +3000; and Macklin Celebrini's San Jose Sharks at +3500. The longest odds: the Vancouver Canucks and Calgary Flames, both at +100000.

Trade demands granted ... and ignored
The NHL is in an age of player empowerment and that was never more evident than during this offseason. A half dozen players requested trades from their current teams, directly or indirectly. Some of those requests were granted. Some were not, leading to uncomfortable times for three American Olympians.

The Ottawa Senators traded captain Brady Tkachuk to the Panthers, where he finally unites with his brother and podcast co-host Matthew. Brady Tkachuk claimed his trade request was fueled by a desire to play for a Cup contender in Florida, which he helped force with his trade protection. Senators owner Michael Andlauer had another take: "Blood is thicker than water, and let's just say that his father and his brother got in his kitchen," he told The Athletic.

Goalie Connor Hellebuyck is another gold medal winner seeking an exit from a Canadian franchise. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner, considered the best goalie in hockey, informed the Jets he wanted to be traded after last season, despite the 33-year-old being under contract through 2030-31. His no-movement clause limits the field, and the Jets haven't found an offer yet to their satisfaction.

Both the Jets and Hellebuyck released statements before training camp acknowledging the stalemate. He's currently suspended from the team and will begin losing salary on opening night. The Jets say the door is open for him to remain with Winnipeg.

Dylan Larkin, another U.S. national team player, had his trade request with the Detroit Red Wings go public late last season, despite having five years left on his contract. Multiple reports claimed that Larkin, who has a no-trade clause, limited his desired destinations to Minnesota, Florida and Vegas. Detroit has yet to fulfil that request, and in the process saw GM Steve Yzerman step away from that role. Larkin reported to Red Wings camp and was stripped of his captaincy.

Finally, U.S. Olympian Zach Werenski, who won the Norris Trophy as the NHL's top defenseman last season, reportedly informed the Columbus Blue Jackets that he didn't intend to sign an extension with the team when his contract is up in summer 2028. GM Don Waddell took the proactive approach and tried to trade Werenski to the Dallas Stars, only to have Werenski block the trade with his no-movement clause.

As all of this was made public to fans, Werenski and the team released statements in July that attempted to defuse the situation. Werenski said that "everything got blown out of proportion" and reaffirmed his commitment to win in Columbus, which has missed the playoffs in six straight seasons.

Two other players were more successful in their trade requests. Defenseman Darnell Nurse told the Edmonton Oilers he wanted a change of scenery after 12 seasons, and they sent him to San Jose. Defenseman Simon Nemec, the second overall pick in the 2022 draft, had his long-standing desire to move on granted by the New Jersey Devils, who sent the restricted free agent to the Calgary Flames.

Other faces in new places
Some of the big names that moved on to new teams this season include:

Center Vincent Trocheck, whom the New York Rangers (finally) traded to the Utah Mammoth in a deal that included defenseman Sean Durzi. Utah also added former New York Islanders captain Anders Lee as a free agent (three years, $5.4 million AAV) and traded winger JJ Peterka to the Boston Bruins after just one season with the franchise.
The Tampa Bay Lightning signed Darren Raddysh to an eight-year deal ($8.5 million AAV) and then shipped him to the Toronto Maple Leafs, who acquired him before Raddysh was expected to be the top unrestricted free agent defenseman on the market.
The Anaheim Ducks traded 23-year-old center Mason McTavish to the St Louis Blues for two first-round picks.
After goalie Sergei Bobrovsky decided to test free agency, the Panthers traded for Devils starting goalie Jacob Markstrom in a deal involving forward Evan Rodrigues.
The Capitals traded for Blues star winger Jordan Kyrou and added Sabres winger Alex Tuch via trade before inking a long-term deal (eight years, $10.5 million AAV).
Former Capitals star John Carlson, who was traded to Anaheim at last season's deadline, signed a two-year deal ($8.5 million AAV) with the Lightning.
Vegas traded leading goal scorer Pavel Dorofeyev to the Rangers, who signed the restricted free agent winger to a seven-year deal ($11 million AAV).
Valeri Nichushkin was acquired via trade by the Blue Jackets from the Avalanche, who added another veteran winger in Jaden Schwartz (three years, $3.25 million AAV).
Goalie Frederik Andersen, the 36-year-old who helped the Hurricanes win the Stanley Cup, became the latest possible solution to the Oilers' goalie issues on a one-year free agent deal ($1 million AAV).
The Chicago Blackhawks acquired puck-moving defenseman Bowen Byram from the Sabres and signed him to a six-year contract extension ($12.5 million AAV). But it's a reunion with another free agent that really captured the hockey world's attention: Franchise icon Patrick Kane is back in Chicago, on a two-year deal ($8 million AAV).

The Leo Carlsson offer sheet drama
If there was one moment that defined the 2026 NHL offseason, it was when Ducks star Leo Carlsson put pen to paper on a five-year, $90 million offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers.

Ducks GM Pat Verbeek said he anticipated there could be an offer sheet tendered to the 21-year-old center ... just not one that massive. "Did we expect the offer sheet to be this high? No. We did not see that one coming," he said.

Verbeek had told his peers that Anaheim ownership would match any offer sheet given to Carlsson, and the Ducks did just that to keep their young center from bolting to Philly.

But the reverberations from that signing were felt all over the league -- and within the Ducks' own roster. Anaheim signed defenseman Pavel Mintyukov (five years, $7.2 million AAV) to avoid any potential poaching, and handed 22-year-old Cutter Gauthier a six-year deal with a $13.5 million AAV after Carlsson raised his price.

The mega-extensions
Carlsson's offer sheet deal gave him the largest cap hit in the history of the NHL ... for about a minute. Macklin Celebrini, the 20-year-old San Jose Sharks phenom, signed a five-year extension that begins in 2027-28 and carries an $18.8 million cap hit. But about a month after that, Colorado defenseman Cale Makar became the first $20 million AAV player of the salary cap era, signing an eight-year extension worth $163.2 million that begins in 2027-28.

Other young stars that signed big extensions included Chicago's Connor Bedard (five years, $15 million AAV) and Columbus center Adam Fantilli (six years, $13.75 million AAV).

Had he agreed to play for the Seattle Kraken, Jason Robertson could have joined the mega-contract club, too. Multiple reports stated that the Kraken would have given the restricted free agent winger eight years and upward of $15 million annually, but Robertson wouldn't agree to a sign-and-trade. Instead, he and the Stars ended a prolonged contract standoff with a one-year, $12 million deal that keeps the 45-goal scorer in Dallas before unrestricted free agency next summer.

Two contract situations are dominating the discourse as the season begins. There's Minnesota defenseman Quinn Hughes, who can become an unrestricted free agent next summer. What's his desire to try and win a Stanley Cup with the Wild versus potentially playing with his brothers in New Jersey? There's also Nikita Kucherov, who won NHL MVP for the second time last season. The Tampa Bay star winger can become an unrestricted free agent next summer.

The coaching (and GM) carousel
There was plenty of movement off the ice as well since last season, from the bench to the boardroom.

Five teams named new head coaches. Former Kings coach Jim Hiller replaced Craig Berube in Toronto, with the well-traveled Peter Laviolette taking over in Los Angeles. AHL coach Ryan Craig is the bench boss in Vegas after replacing John Tortorella, who took over with eight games left in the 2025-26 season and led the Golden Knights to the Stanley Cup Final. Former Canucks player Manny Malhotra earned his first NHL head coaching gig with Vancouver, replacing Adam Foote.

But the most notable hiring came in Edmonton, where Mike Babcock made an unlikely return to the NHL to succeed Kris Knoblauch.

Babcock, a Stanley Cup champion who has been accused of mental abuse by multiple former players, resigned from the Blue Jackets in 2023 before ever coaching a game for them, after his requests to look at personal photos from players' phones drew criticism. But the Oilers turned to Babcock after the Golden Knights refused to let former coach Bruce Cassidy -- who was still under contract -- fill the Edmonton job opening. The NHL investigated Babcock's time with Columbus, found "no current basis to restrict his employment," and cleared the way for Edmonton to hire him.

What makes the situation ever more peculiar is that the Oilers' veterans leaders -- Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Zach Hyman -- drove the effort to hire Babcock, having vetted the controversial coach personally.

The NHL saw several changes among general managers, too. Colorado's Chris MacFarland left to take over the Nashville Predators from Barry Trotz; that led to Joe Sakic, whom MacFarland replaced with the Avalanche, moving back in as general manager. Ryan Johnson (Vancouver), Sunny Mehta (New Jersey) and Alex Steen (St. Louis) became first-time general managers. Shawn Horcoff became the interim GM in Detroit when Steve Yzerman abruptly stepped down after seven seasons. And former Arizona Coyotes GM John Chayka was named the new head of hockey operations for the Maple Leafs.

Turning over new leafs in Toronto
The Maple Leafs had a transformative offseason, having missed the playoffs for the first time in 10 seasons and still searching for their first Stanley Cup win since 1967.

After Toronto dismissed general manager Brad Treliving, the team stunned fans with his replacements: Chayka, who left the NHL after resigning as Coyotes general manager in 2020; and Maple Leafs Hall of Fame player Mats Sundin, who was brought on as a senior executive adviser in hockey operations. Chayka then hired Hiller, who was fired after 59 games by the Kings last season, to replace Berube.

On the ice, Chayka made more than a dozen moves to reshape the Leafs' roster behind returning stars Auston Matthews and William Nylander. He acquired Darren Raddysh in a sign-and-trade with Tampa Bay. He signed several free agents, most prominently goalie Sergei Bobrovsky of the Panthers and Jack Roslovic from the Oilers. Chayka also picked up forward Nicholas Paul from the Lightning.

The team's most intriguing acquisition arrived courtesy of its NHL draft lottery win: Gavin McKenna, the Penn State winger selected first overall in June.

Rookie class of 2026-27
McKenna is part of a deep rookie class at forward. It's led by Philadelphia Flyers winger Porter Martone, who was a late-season star for them during Philly's playoff run. It's a class that also includes:

Sharks winger Ivar Stenberg, the second overall pick in June's draft
Blackhawks center Anton Frondell, the third overall pick in 2025, and winger Roman Kantserov, a point-per-game player in the KHL
Bruins center James Hagens, the Boston College player drafted seventh overall in 2025
Capitals forward Ilya Protas, brother of Capitals winger Aliaksei Protas
Sabres forward Konsta Helenius, who was an energizing presence as a late-season reinforcement

The top rookie defenseman is Washington's Cole Hutson, whose brother Lane is a star for the Canadiens. In goal, there are rookies worth monitoring: Montreal's Jacob Fowler and Pittsburgh's Sergei Murashov.

New CBA goes into effect
The new four-year collective bargaining agreement between the NHL and the NHLPA officially kicked in on Sept. 16, although some of its rules were fast-tracked in last season. Among the rules that kicked in this month:

An 84-game season, with two additional games added to the schedule thanks to a shorter preseason. NHL opening night is Sept. 29, the first time since 1993 that the league is opening its full regular season in September.
Long-term contracts are capped at seven years for a player re-signing with their current team and six years if they sign a contract with another club.
The total signing bonus money across a contract is capped at 60% of the total value of the deal. Leo Carlsson's offer sheet contract -- signed before the new rules kicked in -- had $85.3 million of his $90 million paid in bonus money, or around 95% of the total compensation.
Every team will now have its own emergency backup goalie (EBUG) who will travel with the team. These goalies can't have played in the NHL before under contract, can't have more than 80 games of pro experience and can't have played professionally anywhere in the past three seasons. Expect most of them to be team staff members.

Farewell skate for Alex Ovechkin?
It didn't feel like goodbye for Alex Ovechkin after last season, his 21st in the NHL. The league's all-time leading goal scorer with 929 tallies, Ovechkin said he was "pretty sure" the Capitals' season finale wasn't his last game and that his children wanted him to continue playing. But he did want to make sure that he was returning to an improved Washington team, after the Capitals missed the playoffs last season.

After a busy start to the offseason for Washington, Ovechkin officially announced he'd return for another NHL campaign, signing a one-year contract with a base salary of $1 million and bonus money that brings his compensation to $9 million.

The 41-year-old captain's return for a 22nd season was overshadowed in the preseason by his controversial appearance in a video for Russian President Vladimir Putin's political party. Capitals general manager Chris Patrick told ESPN's Robert Klemko that if Ovechkin had told the team he planned to film the ad, "we would have worked to avoid the situation very hard."

Finally, expansion is on the NHL's radar
While the NHL is not officially in an expansion phase, commissioner Gary Bettman said the league has received "expressions of interest" about landing a new franchise.

That interest is most intense in Texas. In June, the Friedkin family began a six-month process to evaluate Houston and Austin as potential locations for a second NHL team in the state, joining the Dallas Stars. At the time, Bettman said it would take an approximately $3.5 billion investment to acquire a franchise, including an expansion fee and the cost of the new arena.

There are three groups in Atlanta that have discussed a bringing an expansion franchise there. It would be the third time the NHL has put a team in A-Town; the Flames moved to Calgary and the Thrashers moved to Winnipeg.

Also seeking another chance at an NHL franchise: Phoenix, where the NHL has talked with multiple groups about a successor to the defunct Coyotes. But Bettman said, "It doesn't make sense to talk about it" unless there are firm plans to build an arena there."

Expect further clarity on expansion at December's board of governors meeting. But keep in mind that along with where these teams might play and who will own them, there are some NHL owners that aren't completely sold on adding a 33rd and 34th team to the league. After all, it's hard enough to win the Cup with 31 other opponents as it stands.

stories.headline: Chelsea charged by FA over alleged discriminatory chanting
stories.summary: Chelsea have been charged by the Football Association after discriminatory chanting was reported during their Premier League game away at Fulham in August.
stories.body:
Chelsea have been charged by the Football Association after discriminatory chanting was reported during their Premier League game away at Fulham in August.

Following the team's 3-2 win over their west London rivals on the season's opening weekend, the club issued a statement to their fans warning them against "sectarian chanting."

Victory at Craven Cottage came courtesy of goals from João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer but the club have now been charged with failing to ensure the behaviour of their supporters.

An FA statement read: "Chelsea FC has been charged with breaching FA Rule E21 during the ninth minute of its Premier League fixture against Fulham FC on 24 August.

"It's alleged that the club failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way. It's further alleged that this behaviour was discriminatory in that it included a reference, whether express or implied, to religion or belief."

The day after the match, Chelsea issued a statement to fans who had been in attendance, which read: "The passion and backing from our fans are vital in achieving a successful season, and we encourage you to continue your vocal support for the team.

"Following the fixture, we have received multiple reports of sectarian chanting from a small portion of those in attendance at the match.

- Transfer value tiers: Which club has the most players worth £100M-plus?

- Andre Villas-Boas hits back at John Terry's plane story: 'I see it different'

- Estêvão on reduced game time at Chelsea: 'I try to seize every opportunity I have'

"We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic. Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium.

"Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us tackle discriminatory chanting."

stories.headline: Sun mark franchise's last game in Connecticut with victory, joy
stories.summary: Playing for nothing but pride, the Sun prevailed 95-81 in their final game before the franchise's impending relocation to Houston, marking the final moments of the organization's 24-season history with celebration and joy.
stories.body:
UNCASVILLE, Conn. -- The past 13 months for the Connecticut Sun and their fans have been ones of confusion and heartache as the franchise's sale and relocation went from possibility to reality, all while wins on the court became more difficult to come by.

But the final moments of the organization's storied 24-season history in Connecticut will be remembered as ones of celebration, joy and winning.

The Sun prevailed 95-81 on Thursday over the Toronto Tempo in their final game before the franchise's impending relocation to Houston, bringing a sellout crowd of 8,911 at Mohegan Sun Arena to its feet as the clock ticked down to zero.

The Sun had just 10 wins on the season entering Thursday and had dropped six straight. A loss against Toronto would have ensured them the best odds at the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft.

But the young, rebuilding Sun knew they were playing Thursday for more than what any numbers or records could reflect.

"Coach spoke about us playing for our pride -- pride for our fans, pride for our name, pride for the organization itself," said guard Ashlon Jackson, whose 3-pointer with 51 seconds remaining marked the final points in franchise history. "I think we did just that."

Even once the final buzzer sounded, the fans did not want to leave. They watched the team gather for one final photo at half court. They watched WNBA legend Brittney Griner take the Sun flag and run around the floor before going around and high-fiving fans sitting courtside.

They watched Aaliyah Edwards, who starred collegiately at nearby UConn, declare on the postgame broadcast, "This is the basketball capital of the world, baby! Don't ever forget!"

Team president Jen Rizzotti -- a self-described Connecticut girl and UConn legend who will move with the team to Houston -- then addressed the crowd, revealing fans would be permitted to stay in the arena well after the game ended to get autographs from the players.

"You've never disappointed," Rizzotti said through tears. "You've proved that Connecticut deserves a WNBA team. And I just want you all to know that no matter what happens from here, this team, as they move onto the next chapter of their careers, the success that all of them have in their future, you will always be a part of that. Always."

Unlike previous WNBA franchises that relocated or folded abruptly, the Sun's sale and relocation was rather drawn out. The team initially tried to sell the franchise to an ownership group in Boston last summer before that was blocked by the league. The sale to the Fertitta family and relocation to Houston was eventually announced in March, allowing the Sun to commemorate the franchise's history all summer, including by honoring several former players and coaches at games as part of their Sun Legends program.

But the finality of it all started to hit Rizzotti the past few weeks after returning from the FIBA break. On Thursday, it was unavoidable.

"Today feels different," she told ESPN before the game. "We've known this was coming, but it's actually here, and it's the last time we're going to put on a show."

The Sun became Connecticut's only major professional sports team in 2003 when the Mohegan Tribe bought what was the Orlando Miracle and relocated the team to Uncasville, Connecticut.

Despite being in such a small market, the franchise found a way to be successful on the court, recording 16 playoff berths and four Finals appearances, most recently in 2019 and 2022.

"The Mohegan Tribe bought a team when it wasn't popular to own a WNBA team," Rizzotti told ESPN on Thursday. "They supported it and invested in it at times where it wasn't profitable, and they were at the forefront of treating the players a certain way. Even building the facility that they did for us to practice in. Although things have passed us by, I don't want people to forget what the tribe did to bring a team here and support it for two decades.

"I don't think you talk about the WNBA without the Connecticut Sun and what it's meant on the court and the players that have played here and the sustained success that it had for such a long time."

With the Sun moving to Houston, the possibility of another WNBA team returning to New England -- where Connecticut has served as women's basketball hub since the 1990s -- remains unclear.

"A lot of our emotion comes from we feel like we're leaving this void [in the community]," Rizzotti said. "But we also feel proud that we're leaving a legacy of giving back to the state that's given us so much."

But the Sun gave their fans a final show to remember as young standouts Jackson, Edwards, Raegan Beers, Hailey Van Lith and Gianna Kneepkens fueled a 57-point second half that allowed Connecticut to comfortably pull away and keep the energy high at Mohegan Sun Arena.

"Tonight they played with pride," Connecticut coach Rachid Meziane said. "But I also saw a team playing with a lot of joy, and it's also why I am very proud of them ... as a coach, it was very important for me to finish the season like that."

Added Edwards: "Going through such a tough season like we did, I know it was supposed to be our 'Sunset Season,' we were trying to chase a championship, and some of us are holding our heads down on that.

"But ultimately, we're holding our heads up high because we were part of a legacy. We were part of the impact, and everyone today and before today made history by just pouring into a franchise when no one else would."

stories.headline: NBA Rank 2026: League execs examine top 100 countdown, race for No. 1
stories.summary: ESPN's NBA Rank 2026 countdown is in the books, but debates are just beginning -- on social media and around the league.
stories.body:
Nothing in the NBA world inspires heated debate like ESPN's annual ranking of the 100 players for the upcoming season.

After NBA Rank 2026 came out earlier this week, New York Knicks guard Josh Hart unleashed a little sarcasm in response to landing at No. 89.

"They [are] always wrong," Hart wrote on social media. "I should be at least No. 88."

The newly minted champion was hardly the only person in the league to raise objections with the results during a year that lacked consensus.

With help from an informal survey of a dozen NBA executives and league personnel, let's run through some of the biggest ranking arguments and critiques that emerged this week to set the table for the 2026-27 season and clear up misconceptions.

NBA Rank 2026:

Top 10 players | Nos. 11-50 | Nos. 51-100

Roundtable: Was LeBron ranked too low?

Top 100 audit: What NBA Rank got wrong

10 players already on the radar for 2027

The battle for No. 1

ESPN's seven-person voting panel was split between three players for the No. 1 spot: Nikola Jokic prevailed with 694 points in the vote, narrowly topping Victor Wembanyama (693) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (691).

Similarly, the survey of front office executives returned passionate arguments for all three players to be considered the best in the world.

Jokic's supporters highlighted his statistical production and offensive orchestration, while Wembanyama's fans pointed to his two-way impact and San Antonio's 62-win season in 2025-26, and Gilgeous-Alexander's backers focused on his back-to-back MVP awards and leadership.

"Jokic makes his whole team better than anyone else," one general manager said. "If you gave him and Wemby the same teammates, Denver would be better. Wemby being young doesn't bother me. What bothers me is that he made young mistakes in the playoffs."

Still, plenty of league executives agreed with ESPN's insiders that the 22-year-old Wembanyama's time is now.

"Look at how fast he is improving," one general manager said. "If you're looking ahead to where we'll be [after the 2027 playoffs], he's got to be No. 1. He could be No. 1 for the next five years."

With Jokic posting triple-doubles and Wembanyama leading the NBA in several defensive metrics, a Gilgeous-Alexander backer argued that the conversation should be about more individual numbers.

"He's the most complete player in the world," the executive said. "Production, leadership, emotional intelligence. List all the boxes that a star should check, and he checks the most."

Two more No. 1 candidates

After Jokic, Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander, ESPN's voting panel had a noticeable gap before the second tier, which included Luka Doncic at No. 4 and Giannis Antetokounmpo at No. 5.

Though most of the informal survey respondents agreed with the main three candidates, one league executive argued that Doncic should be included in the top tier and will end the season at No. 1.

"With LeBron [James] gone, the weight and expectations of the [Los Angeles] Lakers will push Luka to reach his full potential," he said. "He will take the MVP trophy home to Slovenia next summer."

Another respondent expected Antetokounmpo to regain his MVP status after an offseason trade sent him from the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat.

"Revenge mission," he said. "People took him for granted in Milwaukee. You can't ignore him in Miami."

Lottery reform impact

Multiple team executives predicted that the NBA's lottery reform will prompt a wave of reevaluations across the ESPN list.

With teams no longer incentivized to lose games in volume to improve their draft positioning, executives expect player participation to increase across the board. In turn, they expect more competitive games and more parity in the standings.

The Jazz, Pacers and Wizards were mentioned as teams with players whose perceived value could improve substantially in a post-tanking reality.

"No one talks about you if you don't play or if you play and lose by 20 every night," one executive said. "But that can change overnight."

Addressing NBA Rank's critics

Let's shift gears to run through some hot-button topics that emerged on social media following NBA Rank's release. (Note: The posts have been lightly edited for clarity.)

OG Anunoby and the Knicks

"Worst of all is OG Anunoby at No. 34. Behind Jalen Johnson and James Harden of all people who were overwhelmed no-shows in the [Knicks] series."

Without a doubt, Anunoby's stock is at an all-time high after he helped the Knicks clinch the NBA championship with one of the most iconic shots in league history. The veteran forward had a phenomenal run through the playoffs, emerging as New York's second-highest scorer while shooting 48.9% on 3-pointers and providing excellent defense across multiple positions.

ESPN's voters base their rankings on a variety of factors such as overall production, team success, health, age, role and consistency rather than head-to-head performance in a single playoff series.

Anunoby's ranking appeared to reflect skepticism among some voters over how well his team would perform if he had to handle a larger role on offense as a playmaker or distributor. With Jalen Brunson in place as an elite high-usage engine and Karl-Anthony Towns spacing the court as a dependable secondary scorer, Anunoby is free to live his best life.

If Anunoby switched spots with Atlanta's Jalen Johnson, would he be able to scale his production to match Johnson's impressive numbers? Anunoby's prior stint with the Toronto Raptors suggests there's a hard ceiling to what you can expect from him on offense.

Walker Kessler and the Lakers

"Walker Kessler at No. 73 is a textbook example of the 'Prestige Zone' effect: Literally hasn't played basketball in a year, but he still jumped 25 spots in the rankings because he was traded to the Lakers."

This was a very popular complaint: How did Kessler improve so much from last year's rankings after playing only five games during the 2025-26 season due to shoulder surgery? Surely, this must be evidence of ESPN's pro-Lakers agenda.

First, remember that this is a forward-looking list for the 2026-27 season rather than a recap of last year. Second, it must be noted that Kessler was traded from a Jazz team that ranked below average in offensive efficiency in each of the past three years to a Lakers team led by Doncic, one of the NBA's best playmakers.

Kessler's offensive game is derivative: 67% of his baskets during his first four seasons were assisted by his teammates. It's reasonable to expect him to perform substantially better as an offensive player with Doncic in Los Angeles than he did before his shoulder injury when Collin Sexton and an unproven Keyonte George were Utah's lead guards.

Back in his Dallas Mavericks days, Doncic brought the best out of derivative centers such as Daniel Gafford and Dereck Lively II. Assuming Kessler stays healthy, there's a decent chance he'll outperform his No. 73 ranking.

Jayson Tatum and the Celtics

"Jayson Tatum is fresh off an Achilles tear, stunk when he returned to the court, and choked a 3-1 lead against the 76ers but doesn't get moved down at all. Joel Embiid single-handedly led the 3-1 comeback against Tatum, but he gets ranked 30 spots lower because injuries only matter when it's convenient."

Tatum was indeed one of the trickiest players to rank: The Celtics forward landed at No. 9, a noticeable drop from his No. 5 ranking in his last healthy season two years ago. To be clear, the version of Tatum that returned to the court in March wasn't close to a top-10 player.

ESPN's voters appeared willing to look past his bumpy return because it came so quickly after his original injury in May 2025. By the time the 2026-27 season starts, Tatum will have had almost 18 months to recover. If post-Achilles Tatum performs like post-Achilles Kevin Durant, his inclusion in the top 10 will be proved correct. But that's no guarantee.

The comparison to Embiid falls short because of their disparate health track records: Tatum is recovering from the first major injury of his career and has logged at least 70 games in six of his nine seasons, while Embiid is chronically hurt and has never appeared in 70 games in the 12 seasons since he was drafted. Tyrese Maxey also might have something to say about Embiid "single-handedly" leading Philadelphia's playoff comeback.

Donovan Mitchell and the Cavaliers

"Are we sure Mitchell is still a top-10 player in the league?"

Mitchell's inclusion at No. 10 seemed to receive more pushback online than any of the other rankings for the NBA's top-tier stars. But why? Mitchell was selected to the All-NBA second team, he finished seventh in MVP voting, and he was one of only six players to average at least 27 points, four rebounds and five assists per game while appearing in at least 60 games last season.

What's more, Mitchell's career reached a new peak when he led the Cleveland Cavaliers to his first conference finals appearance. Cleveland was one of only nine teams to win 50 games last season, and Mitchell was the steadying presence with Jarrett Allen battling injuries and Darius Garland traded for Harden during the season.

The arguments against Mitchell tend to focus on his lack of size and limited playoff success, though it's worth pointing out that he's led playoff teams in each of the past nine seasons. Two key differentiators between Mitchell and some prominent names who finished behind him on the list were his age and availability: Stephen Curry (No. 12), Kevin Durant (No. 13) and LeBron James (No. 18) are all much more famous and accomplished than Mitchell, but they combined to appear in four playoff wins last season.

Meanwhile, Curry (age 38) and James (age 41) missed far more time due to injuries than Mitchell (age 30).

Finally, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown both had strong cases to make the top 10, but ESPN's voting panel likely favored Mitchell because Cleveland advanced further in the 2026 playoffs than Maxey's 76ers and Brown's Celtics. Maxey and Brown could also see their individual statistics take a hit in 2026-27 now that they're teammates with James and Embiid on the souped-up 76ers.

Four rookies in the top 100

"Stop [including] rookies who haven't played a single second of regular season basketball in top-100 players in the league lists."

There's a lot of merit to this viewpoint. Comparing stats from college or international basketball to NBA production is an inexact science, and having an equitable baseline is essential to comparative analysis.

However, recent rookies such as Wembanyama and Cooper Flagg have left no doubt that they belong in the top 100. For years, smart list makers were careful not to be overly bullish on young players because they were bound to endure some struggles early in their NBA transitions. Now, pundits must caution against being too pessimistic because plenty of prospects -- including Wembanyama, Flagg, Kon Knueppel and VJ Edgecombe -- have hit the ground running in their first seasons.

The top four players from the 2026 class -- AJ Dybantsa (No. 78), Darryn Peterson (No. 83), Cameron Boozer (No. 85) and Caleb Wilson (No. 97) -- were included in this year's NBA Rank. Realistically, having four rookies on the list seems aggressive.

Fast forward to April, though, and there's a very good chance that at least two of those four will be regarded as no-brainer top 100 talents. Would banning all of them from this conversation be fair?

stories.headline: Suspended Swans in running for club best-and-fairest
stories.summary: Isaac Heeney is on track to be crowned the Sydney Swans' club champion after the AFL club ruled out changing the eligibility criteria for its best-and-fairest award.
stories.body:
Isaac Heeney is on track to be crowned the Sydney Swans' club champion after the AFL club ruled out changing the eligibility criteria for its best-and-fairest award.

But midfielder Heeney won't attend the awards night next week, requesting to skip the event along with Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice.

The five served a club-imposed ban from August, including the Swans' finals campaign, for breaching club standards following a post-AFL match party at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

Heeney and fellow ball-winner Warner are the frontrunners -- ahead of ruck Brodie Grundy -- for the club's Bob Skilton Medal, which will be presented at Sydney Town Hall next Thursday.

The club confirmed on Friday that eligibility and voting criteria will remain unchanged, leaving all players who represented the Swans this season eligible to win the award.

Heeney has won the club's last two best-and-fairest awards, while Warner finished runner-up to Callum Mills in 2022.

The AFL also opted against ruling out Heeney and Warner for the Brownlow Medal, but did not invite the pair to last Monday night's awards dinner at Crown Palladium.

The five players were made ineligible for All-Australian honours.

It comes after the five earlier this week returned to Swans headquarters for the first time since August, individually offering apologies to colleagues and teammates.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media on Wednesday, doing so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," he said on Wednesday evening.

"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Warner spoke upon arriving at headquarters and said he was "just here for my exit interview".

Their club-imposed suspensions are separate from a police investigation into sexual assault allegations.

No charges have been laid, and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the suspended players. Bice was subsequently cleared by police.

All five are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Blakey is reportedly seeking a trade to Victorian rivals, but football boss Leon Cameron had dismissed those rumblings as "speculation" earlier this month.

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident -- which was first flagged on September 2 -- takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

stories.headline: Goose at Dodger Stadium during Padres-Dodgers recalls past wildlife interruptions
stories.summary: A goose slid on Dodger Stadium's field during Padres-Dodgers. It's not the first time a creature stole the show at a sporting event.
stories.body:
Sports are great. Animals are great. When the two mix, it's incredible -- sometimes.

Fans at Dodger Stadium witnessed an unlikely instance of such a mix Wednesday, when a goose flew onto the field and slid stomach first in memorable fashion.

This wasn't close to the first time an animal has become part of the game during a sporting event. There was the time a sportswriter's dog ran onto the field, interrupting a Georgia football game. And San Antonio seemingly has had as many bat encounters as "Dracula."

In honor of these amazing incidents, let's look back at some other top animal-on-field moments.

What: Goose

Where: Chicago

When: 2026

A goose patrolled the field in the bottom of the third inning during the Cubs' game against the Phillies in April. Play continued and Cubs first baseman Michael Busch recorded a hit. The baseball flew over the goose, prompting the animal to fly away.

What: Dog

Where: Tesero, Italy

When: 2026

During the Winter Olympics, a local Czechoslovakian wolfdog named Nazgul managed to get away from his owner's sight and dash onto the homestretch of the cross-country ski course in Lago di Tesero -- during the race. Luckily, there was no serious disruption to the race, a preliminary qualifying round, spare for a few seconds of confusion shaved off the times of active racers who witnessed Nazgul's trot.

"I was like, 'Am I hallucinating?'" said Tena Hadzic, a 21-year-old Croatian skier who was among the participants whose time on the homestretch portion of the race coincided with the dog. "I don't know what I should do, because maybe he could attack me, bite me."

Nazgul was quickly corralled and returned home, but not before he endeared himself to spectators and viewers back home.

What: Squirrel

Where: New York, New York

When: 2025

A squirrel emerged in the fourth inning of a Yankees-Red Sox rivalry game from behind home plate, stopping right at Jhostynxon Garcia's left foot. The rodent took off again and stopped at the third-base foul line before attempting to dig a hole in front of the mound and then scampering down the right-field line to search for a way out.

What: Squirrel

Where: Detroit, Michigan

When: 2025

The squirrel scampered around the outfield, eventually making its way to the warning track before climbing into the Tigers' bullpen during the first inning of the San Francisco Giants-Detroit Tigers match.

What: Snake

Where: Charlotte, North Carolina

When: 2025

Golfers and patrons had a front-row experience with the entanglement of sports and animals during the second round of the 2025 PGA Championship when a snake disrupted the contest.

The snake slithered its way through the course -- with the ball seemingly being its target before moving past it.

What: Bunny

Where: Norman, Oklahoma

When: 2025

During a college baseball matchup at L. Dale Mitchell Park, a bunny disrupted the contest.

With two outs in the top of the fourth inning, a bunny appeared on the third-base side. The animal started running around behind home plate before heading toward the bullpen and exiting swiftly.

What: Squirrel

Where: Oxford, Mississippi

When: 2024

Ole Miss and Oklahoma were interrupted during an SEC meeting at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium by a squirrel that disrupted the game.

Toward the end of the first quarter, a squirrel took the field on the 17-yard line before running to the end zone for a touchdown and into the tunnel away from action.

What: Insect

Where: New York City

When: 2024

Frances Tiafoe and Grigor Dimitrov had a front-row experience during their quarterfinal match at the 2024 US Open when an insect disrupted the contest.

Tiafoe pointed out the black insect during the dead ball as the ball boys sprinted onto the court and spent around 30 seconds trying to contain it by hand before the match resumed.

What: Raccoon

Where: Chester, Pennsylvania

When: 2024

The Philadelphia Union and New York City FC had a friendly creature that caused a brief stoppage in play at Subaru Park in Philadelphia.

A raccoon strolled onto the field midway through the first half. It proceeded to evade workers that attempted to remove it. However, after 161 seconds, the raccoon was taken off the field.

What: Turtle

Where: Bradenton, Florida

When: 2024

The Bradenton Marauders, a minor league affiliate of the Pittsburgh Pirates, were in the middle of their game when a turtle caused a brief stoppage in play. The surprisingly fast reptile roamed around the outfield for a bit before pitcher Magdiel Cotto managed to safely remove it from play.

What: Bees

Where: Chase Field, Arizona

When: 2024

Ahead of a game against the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Arizona Diamondbacks received a few surprise visitors behind home plate -- bees.

There was a colony forming on the protective netting behind home plate, which resulted in a delay of one hour and 55 minutes, according to the Diamondbacks.

The Diamondbacks had to call beekeeper Matt Hilton from Blue Sky Pest Control.

Hilton said he was at his son's T-ball game when he got the call. Little did he know he'd instantly become a fan favorite after taking care of the bees.

"I thought I was just here to take care of a bee problem, and people were pretty hyped up," Hilton told MLB Network.

Hilton also threw out the ceremonial first pitch.

What: Cat

Where: Angel Stadium, California

When: 2024

There's something about the last day of April and animals on the diamond.

On the same night the Diamondbacks were dealing with bees, the Los Angeles Angels and Philadelphia Phillies got a surprise visit from a cat.

In the bottom of the seventh, the cat sprinted and landed in the Phillies' dugout. Thankfully, as the broadcaster pointed out, it wasn't a black cat.

What: Squirrel

Where: Yankees Stadium, New York

When: 2023

Early in the 2023 season, a squirrel astounded the Yankee Stadium faithful when it ran across the outfield wall.

Fortunately, it appears neither fan nor squirrel were harmed in the little creature's big adventure.

What: Bats

Where: AT&T Center, San Antonio

When: 2009 -- and again in 2019

Here's the thing about bats: If you don't know much about them and what they're capable of, they're terrifying. And at AT&T Center, where the San Antonio Spurs play, they've shown up more than once.

First, we have to go to October 2009, when one bat invaded the Spurs' game against the Sacramento Kings. Luckily, the swift and speedy Manu Ginobili was still on the Spurs, and he was able to somehow swat the creature down and capture it. What's even more interesting is that this happened on Halloween night.

The bats weren't done, though.

The Spurs were taking on the Brooklyn Nets in January when the game was delayed for a few minutes by not just one, but four bats, as the staff worked to clear the animals. Clearly fans knew who was needed, as chants of "Manu, Manu, Manu" broke out in the crowd.

Sorry to break it to you, but the bats weren't done in San Antonio. A month later, during a Spurs game against the New Orleans Pelicans, another bat made its way to the floor at AT&T Center.

This time it was the Spurs' mascot, The Coyote, who was able to capture the critter with a fishing net near the scorer's table during the first quarter. The delay lasted about 90 seconds.

The bats came back again for a third time this year in March when the Spurs were taking on the Milwaukee Bucks. Again, The Coyote came to the rescue.

What: Squirrel

Where: Busch Stadium, St. Louis

When: 2011

Imagine it's your first time bursting into the spotlight, and you win the World Series.

That's how it went down (kind of) for the gray squirrel that ran across home plate at Busch Stadium during Game 3 of the National League Division Series between the Philadelphia Phillies and the St. Louis Cardinals in October 2011.

There was no delay of game, though it was evident that every player was considerably confused.

*Note: We scoured every corner of the interwebs, and there is no original video of the Rally Squirrel. It seems that 2011 was clearly a much simpler time.

The Phillies won Game 3 though, giving them a 2-1 lead in the NLDS. But the Cardinals won Games 4 and 5, clinching the series and heading to the World Series. St. Louis went on to win the 2011 World Series against the Texas Rangers in seven games with Rally Squirrel playing a role.

What: Cat

Where: M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore and MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey

When: 2017, 2019

Cats are pretty nimble creatures, so it's no surprise how often they make their way into any sports venue.

In 2017, a kitten snuck down into M&T Bank Stadium to take in a game between the Miami Dolphins and the Baltimore Ravens.

Tony Romo's play-by-play is highly entertaining. But the cute cat was eventually captured by stadium staff and taken away.

The story had a happy ending, though. According to the team, a stadium employee officially adopted the stray cat and named her "Rae" -- short for Ravens.

In 2019, a black cat ran onto the field during a New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys "Monday Night Football" game at MetLife Stadium.

What: Dog

Where: Dunhill Links Championship, Scotland

When: 2012

Look, dogs and balls go hand in hand. Not only that, but Scotland is one of the most dog-friendly nations. So, it's no surprise that Dunhill Links has seen its fair share of pooches during golf play.

In 2012, however, one dog took its ball obsession a bit too far and stole Paul Casey's golf ball right off of the third hole green.

"It's the weirdest thing I've ever had happen on a golf course," Casey said. "I noticed the dog on the 12th tee and he sort of followed us down the fairway before taking a real liking to my golf ball."

The good news was that Casey was allowed to play his original ball and scored a birdie on the hole.

What: Bees

Where: Great American Ball Park, Cincinnati

When: 2019

The worst part about bees is you really have no idea which way they are going to fly. And of course, the fact that they can sting you.

There was an 18-minute delay when a swarm of bees landed at the top of the backstop screen before the first pitch of a game in May between the San Francisco Giants and the Cincinnati Reds.

Honestly, we're just glad no one got stung.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail preliminary finals: McLean explains long-term Panthers deal
stories.summary: Isaah Yeo and Moses Leota are both keens to remain Panthers despite interest elsewhere, while Casey McLean is happy for his departing brother.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's preliminary finals weekend.

McLean reveals why he committed long-term to Panthers

Casey McLean has opened up on his decision to commit his long-term future to Penrith, describing his extension through the end of 2030 as another "pinch-me" moment in his rapid rise.

Having grown up in the area and played his junior football with the Panthers, McLean said remaining at the club was an opportunity to repay the faith Penrith showed by handing him his first-grade opportunity.

"Obviously this club, playing for them, growing up my whole life around this area... being able to give back to them, I suppose," McLean said.

"They want me around, but being able to think that I played my juniors here and they want me to stay, that's kind of my way of giving back.

"The coaches and the staff, they gave me my first opportunity to show myself on the big stage, and I think it's just kind of a way I can give back to them as well."

McLean is contracted to Penrith until the end of 2030, positioning the young centre as a key piece of the club's next generation.

McLean opens up on replacing Crichton

Casey McLean has revealed the message from Penrith that helped ease the pressure of stepping into the centre position vacated by Stephen Crichton last year.

McLean admitted he initially arrived in first grade feeling as though he had to replace the premiership-winning centre, before being encouraged to forge his own identity.

"I walked in here thinking... I've got to replace Critta," McLean said.

"But coming here, the boys and coach, they're kind of just like, 'There's no shoes to fill. You've got to take the spot and make it your own, kind of play to your strengths.'

"'You wouldn't be here for no reason. You've worked hard... just be yourself.'"

McLean has since established himself as a key member of Penrith's backline as the Panthers continue transitioning into their next generation.

Leota disappointed to miss Warriors showdown

Moses Leota has admitted there was some disappointment in seeing the Warriors' season come to an end, denying Penrith a potential finals meeting with his former front-row partner James Fisher-Harris.

Leota retains strong ties to New Zealand and spent years forming one of the NRL's premier prop combinations alongside Fisher-Harris at Penrith before the Kiwi international's move across the Tasman.

"They had a really great season," Leota said of the Warriors.

"It's very sad, but it is what it is. There's some weapons in that team, right? They'll get back here next year."

McLean relishing Gagai battle

Casey McLean is preparing for another battle with veteran Knights centre Dane Gagai, declaring the 35-year-old is still performing as though he is in his prime.

McLean has previously spent time around Gagai in representative camp and has also faced the Queensland veteran on several occasions at NRL level.

"He's such an amazing guy," McLean said.

"I don't think he lets his age [affect him]... he still looks like he's in his prime.

"He's still running around, he's still doing what he's doing, leaving his mark on the game.

Yeo and Leota's future

Isaah Yeo has confirmed his preference is to remain at Penrith beyond his current contract, and is hoping to sort out his future following the end of the season.

"It always has been [my preference to stay]," Yeo admitted.

"The idea is to stay at Penrith as a one club player."

Moses Leota has also affirmed his love for Penrith, with the hope a deal gets done following the 2026 finals.

"[Remaining at Penrith] is massive to me," he shared.

"I've been here basically my whole life."

Casey McLean backs brother at Bulldogs

Panthers gun Casey McLean admitted while he's "gutted" that his brother Jesse will be leaving Penrith next year, but he's excited to see him flourish at Canterbury.

"Obviously pretty gutted that we won't be on the same team," he told ESPN.

"It'll be a weird feeling at first, but I'm super excited for the opportunity that he'll be given [at the Bulldogs]."

He went on to vouch for Jesse's ability on the field, expecting his older brother to remind fans of his talent.

"He does talk a little s--- on the field," Casey joked.

"But he's just an amazing player - he helped me grow as well.

"He's such an amazing role model, not only for myself, but for a fair few boys here as well."

Antonelli, who holds an 81-point lead over Russell in the title standings with nine scheduled rounds still remaining, finished 0.351 seconds down on Verstappen.
